newsitem.title: USA: GM March N. American production up 71 pct.
newsitem.headline: GM March N. American production up 71 pct.

text.p: General Motors Corp said it produced 465,000 cars and trucks in North America during March, a 71 percent increase over the automaker's strike-crippled production of 272,000 vehicles in March 1996.

The March output brought GM's total first quarter vehicle production in the United States, Canada and Mexico to 1,442,000 units, an 18.3 percent increase over the 1,219,000 vehicles built in the year-ago period.
GM endured a 17-day strike at two brake plants in Dayton, Ohio, in March 1996, which paralyzed nearly all of the automaker's 29 North American assembly plants.
The strike reduced GM's first quarter 1996 earnings by $900 million. GM has scheduled the release of its first quarter 1997 results for April 14.

GM also said the first quarter production of 1,442,000 vehicles represents an increase of 4,000 units over forecasts released a month ago. GM increased car production by 9,000 units over the prior estimates, while cutting truck production by 5,000 units.

The automaker last month suffered a nearly two week strike at its Fort Wayne, Ind., full-size pickup truck plant. United Auto Workers members struck a GM car plant in Oklahoma City early on Saturday in a walkout that will affect second quarter production.

Nonetheless, GM said its second quarter North American production forecast remains unchanged from estimates released a month ago, at 1,550,000 vehicles. The second quarter forecast represents a 1,000 unit increase over the second quarter of 1996.
